articles.headline: Erling Haaland sets unique goal milestone as Man City beat Sunderland
articles.description: Erling Haaland scored the eighth goal of the game as Manchester City beat Sunderland but it gave him a unique personal record.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland scored the eighth goal of the game as Manchester City beat Sunderland but it gave him a unique personal record.

City won 5-3 on Sunday despite Sunderland's Brian Brobbey netting a hat trick.

Enzo Fernández, Rayan Cherki and two goals from Antoine Semenyo put City ahead before Haaland struck in the 81st minute.

His goal -- initially chalked off due to an offside which VAR overruled -- means he has scored against each of the 25 clubs that he has faced in the Premier League for City.

Previously, Sunderland were the only club he had played but failed to score against. Haaland was goalless in two matches last season against Sunderland.

Haaland's goal against Sunderland was his 117th in the Premier League. His five goals this season puts him top of the Golden Boot chase. Alexander Isak, who scored Liverpool's winner against Bournemouth on Sunday, trails with four goals.

Brobbey, meanwhile, became the first player to score a hat trick and end up losing in the Premier League since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn against Wigan in December 2007. Brobbey was also the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler (vs. Aston Villa in November 1998), Dirk Kuyt (vs. Manchester United in March 2011), and Romelu Lukaku (vs. Manchester United in May 2013).

- Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona track Man City-bound USMNT star Sullivan

- Is Man City teen Samba a backup for Haaland, or new Pogba?

Brobbey is also the first player since Jamie Vardy six years ago to score a hat trick in the Premier League against City. It was the first hat trick in the top flight by a Sunderland player since Jermain Defoe a decade ago.

Meanwhile, City's Enzo Maresca is the sixth manager to win his first five Premier League games in charge of a club, after Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (six), Pep Guardiola at Man City (six), Craig Shakespeare at Leicester (five), Maurizio Sarri at Chelsea (five) and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Man Utd (six).

ESPN Global Research contributed to this report.

Players with early starts

ACTIVE

Joe Burrow, QB, Bengals (back): Burrow dealt with back soreness this week and was listed as questionable but is active and will start. Even in a tough matchup like the Texans, Burrow is a fantasy QB1.

If you want to avoid the matchup, Jaxson Dart and Brock Purdy are realistic options that a fantasy manager could have backing up Burrow. If you're skittish, those two could be started over him. However, for most of you, the choice should be to ride with Burrow.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): After missing the Patriots' opener because of an ankle injury, Henderson returned to practice this week and is active for Week 2. Henderson will share work in the backfield with Rhamondre Stevenson. However, he is the more explosive option and therefore brings more fantasy upside.

Henderson can be played over Quinshon Judkins, MarShawn Lloyd, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, Rico Dowdle, Blake Corum, Kenny Gainwell and Jonathon Brooks.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After a huge Week 1 performance, Coker was limited in practice to start the week because of an ankle injury. He was able to log a full practice Friday and was subsequently removed from the injury report. He is active for Week 2. While the Panthers will not often have scorefests like they did in Week 1, Coker's usage jumps off the screen. He saw nine targets -- three of the deep variety -- and finished with 138 yards and a touchdown, while narrowly missing a second score.

Coker is a high upside WR3. You can feel comfortable playing him over DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr, Alec Pierce, Marvin Harrison Jr and Chris Godwin Jr.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (knee): Kamara is officially active after returning to practice this week. articles.headline: Man City down Sunderland in eight-goal thriller
articles.description: Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100% Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.
articles.body:
Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick in a losing cause as Manchester City maintained their 100% Premier League start with a frantic 5-3 win over Sunderland.

In a game characterized by poor defending, City struggled to slow down the fired-up visitors at the Etihad Stadium, with Brobbey a constant thorn in their side.

Ultimately two goals from Antoine Semenyo and a late strike from Erling Haaland finished the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki were also on target.

Unlike in last week's Manchester derby, City failed to assert control against a Sunderland side clearly not drained by its midweek Europa League excursions.

For new manager Enzo Maresca, however, it was a fifth successive league win and City head into the international break with a three-point lead at the top.

City were given an early warning as Sunderland broke from deep and Enzo Le Fée played in Nilson Angulo but he steered wide.

Sunderland paid for that miss as Fernandez fired home from a ninth-minute free kick after Iliman Ndiaye was brought down by Dayann Methalie.

Goalkeeper Robin Roefs left a huge gap at his near post having set up with only two men in the wall. Fernandez took full advantage, curling in his first goal since his £125 million move from Chelsea.

Sunderland responded quickly and were back level three minutes later as Lee played a superb ball between Rúben Dias and Matheus Nunes and Brobbey deftly flicked beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Sunderland's good work up front contrasted with that at the back, as an attempt to play out plunged them into more trouble. Kevin Danso gifted possession and confusion reigned before Cherki tucked in.

Again City could not hang onto the lead as Le Fée played in Thomas Meunier and his square pass was turned in by Brobbey. The goal was awarded after a lengthy VAR check for offside, leaving Donnarumma to vent his anger at the standard of Cherki's defending.

City regained the lead before the break after a Cherki cross led to more panic in the Sunderland area. The Black Cats claimed Marc Guéhi handled but nothing was given and Semenyo lashed in.

Haaland should have had another but inexplicably missed an open goal after being teed up by Ndiaye and Brobbey was denied another when a shot took an awkward deflection and was palmed onto the bar by Donnarumma.

City's fourth came early in the second half as a Cherki pass intended for Haaland ricocheted off a defender and bobbled into the path of Semenyo. Again he finished clinically.

Yet still City were not convincing and more sloppy play allowed Sunderland back in.

Angulo brought down a long ball as he ran in at the back post and although his effort looked like it might cross the line, Brobbey took no chances and pounced to compete his treble.

Remarkably it could have been 4-4 moments later as Donnarumma failed to deal with a cross and the ball bounced off Dias toward goal. The Portuguese sprinted back to hook off the line.

Haaland finally put the result beyond doubt.

articles.headline: Sources: 49ers owner Jed York won't attend home opener
articles.description: 49ers owner Jed York, who was in Australia but did not attend his team's regular-season opener, also will miss Sunday's home opener in San Francisco against the Dolphins, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
49ers owner Jed York, who was in Australia but did not attend his team's regular-season opener, also will miss Sunday's home opener in San Francisco against the Miami Dolphins, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

York, who was arrested last month on suspicion of engaging in prostitution, is staying away from the Niners so as not to create a distraction, a source told Schefter.

The NFL is expected to make a decision on any potential discipline for York "soon," a source told Schefter.

The Niners opened their season with a 27-7 upset victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, on Sept. 10.

York pleaded no contest on Aug. 24 to a pair of misdemeanor charges after being arrested in Ohio. According to Columbiana County (Ohio) court records obtained by ESPN, York allegedly responded to an undercover ad on a known prostitution website and "arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140."

He was arrested upon arriving at the meeting location with the cellphone used to arrange the meeting, according to the records. York originally was charged with misdemeanor counts of engaging in prostitution and possessing criminal tools, but the former charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct as part of a plea agreement resolving the case.

The NFL said at the time that it was "aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy."

articles.headline: Alexander Isak winner for Liverpool on Andoni Iraola return to Bournemouth
articles.description: Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak's second-half strike secured Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola all three points on his return to the Vitality Stadium in a 1-0 victory over his old club Bournemouth.

The Sweden international broke the deadlock with his fourth goal of the season in the 57th minute after some fine work by Cody Gakpo in the build-up to extend the Reds' unbeaten run and reward Iraola with a second win.

Isak has now already scored more Premier League goals in their first five league matches than he did across his entire previous top-flight campaign.

Iraola left for Anfield after three seasons with the Cherries, capped off by leading the club to a maiden European berth last season.

He was greeted warmly as he emerged before kick-off, exchanging a hug with his German successor Marco Rose.

Liverpool had enjoyed two more days of rest than the hosts, who beat Real Sociedad in San Sebastian on Thursday night to open that historic campaign with a win.

Rose was forced into one change, with Ryan Christie starting in place of Justin Kluivert, who the Cherries boss revealed pre-match had picked up a knock in Spain.

Iraola made three changes from Liverpool's last Premier League outing, starting Gakpo, Milos Kerkez and Alexis Mac Allister in place of Ryan Gravenberch, Víctor Muñoz and Kostas Tsimikas.

Liverpool had an early opportunity when Florian Wirtz was fouled by Tyler Adams, but the resulting 10th-minute free-kick from a dangerous central position was curled into the stands by Dominik Szoboszlai.

It remained a closely-fought contest but lacking chances for either side until Marcus Tavernier broke down the left and picked out Evanilson.

The Brazil striker tried to flick cleverly past Alisson Becker at the near post and nearly had his compatriot beaten, but the Reds goalkeeper reacted just in time with a low palm.

Bradley Barcola's deflected effort just after the half-hour mark finally gave Djordje Petrovic some work to do, the Serbian saving with his leg.

A second Szoboszlai free-kick a few minutes later went closer than his previous attempt, but an opener remained elusive as the Hungarian fizzed it wide.

The game continued in a simliar vein after the break. An alert Adams spared the hosts' blushes after a misplaced pass nearly proved costly, before Christie poked Rayan's cross wide.

But Liverpool breathed life into the match three minutes before the hour with some determined work by Gakpo to muscle his way down the right. His cross was intended for Wirtz, who could not connect under pressure, but Isak, who was lingering nearby, pounced and swept home.

Evanilson tried his luck with just over 20 minutes remaining, but it proved straightforward work for Alisson, who had just come out to punch away Alex Scott's free-kick.

Bournemouth could not make anything out of their late set-pieces, and remain in search of their first Premier League win of the campaign.

articles.headline: Leeds and Crystal Palace battle to gritty goalless draw
articles.body:
Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the season but had to settle for a point from a goalless draw with much-improved Crystal Palace at Elland Road.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin spurned Leeds' best chance when firing straight at Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez in the second half after visiting defender Tyrick Mitchell was denied a winner by VAR.

These are heady times at Leeds after they climbed up to third in the table last week after dismantling Newcastle 4-1 and although they are only five games into their second season back in the top flight, expectation was high among fans before kick-off.

But Palace turned in one of their best displays of the season and will consider themselves unlucky to have secured only one point after creating the better chances.

Given Palace had conceded more goals - 11 - than any other side in the top flight this season, it was no surprise they sat deep when out of possession in the early exchanges.

But they were dangerous on the counter-attack and it took a superb recovery tackle from Tarik Muharemovic to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen, while Leeds squandered early pressure with poor set-piece deliveries.

James Trafford was the first goalkeeper forced into a save when diving low to hold Daichi Kamada's shot and with Leeds struggling to find an end product, Pierre Sage will have been the happier of the two managers at half-time.

Trafford was at full stretch low down to brilliantly turn away Yeremy Pino's free-kick soon after the restart and Kamada's shot flew narrowly wide.

Palace were then denied a deserved lead when Tyrick Mitchell lashed home after Anan Khalaili's cross had deflected off Muharemovic.

Referee Adam Herczeg, taking charge of his first Premier League game, awarded a goal, but it was ruled out by VAR, who deemed Khalaili to have been offside.

Leeds almost snatched the lead after their let-off as Calvert-Lewin fired his point-blank effort from James Justin's cross straight at Palace keeper Benitez.

Palace continued to pose Leeds problems, with midfield lynchpin Adam Wharton central to their promptings while Kamada's header span the wrong side of a post as the home fans grew increasingly frustrated.

Another timely tackle from Muharemovic thwarted Palace substitute Ismaïla Sarr in the penalty area as Leeds failed to carve out another chance against an organised, water-tight defence.
